question.prompt:
Let \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(a_k\) be a finite arithmetic sequence with

\[ a_4+a_7+a_{10}=17 \]

and

\[ \begin{aligned} &a_4+a_5+a_6+\cdots+a_{12}\\ &\quad{}+a_{13}+a_{14}=77. \end{aligned} \] If \(a_k=13,\) then \(k=\)

solutions.explanation:
In an arithmetic sequence, terms equally far from a middle term sum to twice that middle term: the same multiple of the common difference is added on one side and subtracted on the other.

The indices 4 and 10 are equally far from 7, so \(a_4+a_{10}=2a_7\). Hence
\[
3a_7=17,
\qquad a_7=\frac{17}{3}.
\]
There are \(14-4+1=11\) terms in the second sum, with middle term \(a_9\). Pairing \(a_4\) with \(a_{14}\), \(a_5\) with \(a_{13}\), and so on gives five pairs, each summing to \(2a_9\), together with \(a_9\). Thus
\[
11a_9=77,
\qquad a_9=7.
\]
Let \(d\) be the common difference. Moving from index 7 to index 9 takes two steps, so
\[
2d=a_9-a_7
=7-\frac{17}{3}=\frac43,
\qquad d=\frac23.
\]
Starting from \(a_9=7\), the condition \(a_k=13\) becomes
\[
13=7+(k-9)\frac23.
\]
Therefore \(k-9=9\), giving \(\boxed{k=18}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\). This index is compatible with the given terms through \(a_{14}\).
solutions.title: Pair terms around the middle

solutions.explanation:
Let \(a=a_1\) and let \(d\) be the common difference. Expressing every term as \(a_n=a+(n-1)d\) converts the two given sums into two equations for these parameters.

The first condition gives
\[
(a+3d)+(a+6d)+(a+9d)=17,
\]
so \(3a+18d=17\). The second sum has 11 terms, with first term \(a+3d\) and last term \(a+13d\). Using the arithmetic-sequence sum formula gives
\[
\frac{11}{2}\bigl((a+3d)+(a+13d)\bigr)=77,
\]
so \(11a+88d=77\).

Dividing the equations by 3 and 11, respectively, yields
\[
a+6d=\frac{17}{3},
\qquad a+8d=7.
\]
Subtracting eliminates \(a\), giving \(2d=\tfrac43\), so \(d=\tfrac23\). Substitution then gives \(a=\tfrac53\). Therefore
\[
a_k=\frac53+(k-1)\frac23
=\frac{2k+3}{3}.
\]
Setting this equal to 13 gives \(2k+3=39\), hence \(\boxed{k=18}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\). The resulting index is at least 14, as the displayed conditions require.
